_doc: Brand list for the PhishGuard rule engine (src/rules.py): brand_in_subdomain, brand_in_domain, brand_in_path.
Each key is a brand keyword; its value lists the brand's OFFICIAL registered domains (eTLD+1).
A brand rule never fires when the URL's registered domain is one of that brand's official domains.
Matching is by whole token: host labels and paths are split on non-alphanumeric characters.
Keywords shorter than 6 letters must equal a token exactly ('pineapple' does not match 'apple', 'purchase' does not match 'chase').
Keywords of 6+ letters also match as a token PREFIX ('paypalsecure' matches 'paypal').
Keywords of 7+ letters also match as a token SUFFIX ('securepaypal' does not, 'mymicrosoft' does). The 7-letter
suffix limit exists because 'huaweicloud' matched 'icloud' in the train-set review (2026-11-19).
User-content hosts (amazonaws.com, blogspot.com, dropboxusercontent.com, googleusercontent.com) are deliberately NOT
listed as official: attackers can host pages there, so a brand name in their subdomain stays suspicious.
Train-set review (2026-11-19) added missing official domains: apple.com.cn, google.org, aboutamazon.com, aboutamazon.in.
Known limitation: the official lists are not exhaustive. A missing official domain can trigger a brand rule
(a false positive, never a crash). Fan/review sites (apple-history.com) and sites named after a brand
(google.blognewschannel.com) also trigger brand rules: documented false positives.
Edited by hand; never tuned on the test set.
